'use client'

/* GENERATED FILE — do not edit by hand.
 *
 *   node tools/register-silhouettes.mjs
 *
 * Artwork lives in tools/silhouette-art/, the montage order in
 * tools/silhouette-order.json, the framing in tools/register-silhouettes.mjs.
 * Editing this file directly loses the change on the next run and, worse,
 * breaks the registration the whole montage depends on.
 */

/**
 * The fourteen sport silhouettes in the opening montage.
 *
 * Drawn against tools/SILHOUETTE-BRIEF.md, which asked for prop strength over
 * coverage: a sport is recognised by the bow, the bike, the barbell or the bat
 * far more than by the body's shape, and the sports people fail to name —
 * trampoline, surfing — are the ones with no distinctive object.
 *
 * Each athlete is a single `<path>`, all limbs fused into one mass. The prop
 * follows as separate paths and may be stroked. A ground band at opacity 0.45
 * is the one element allowed to be dimmer than the figure.
 *
 * Every figure carries a translation measured in a real browser. At roughly
 * 150ms a frame the eye does not see fourteen pictures, it sees one figure
 * changing, so anything that moves between frames reads as motion — an
 * unregistered set makes the athlete jump around the screen and turns a morph
 * into a flicker book. The pass centres the athlete, then backs off wherever
 * doing so would push a prop out of shot. Elements the artwork already draws
 * past the frame edge — ground bands, oars, the barbell — were meant to bleed
 * and do not constrain the placement.
 *
 * The order alternates facing direction so consecutive frames read as one
 * figure turning rather than as a stamp repeated, opens on the tallest and
 * least ambiguous figure, and closes on the only front-facing one, arms
 * overhead, which is where the mark rises from.
 *
 * They render in --ink-figure, which is a safety constraint rather than a
 * style choice: at montage speed these are large-area elements changing faster
 * than three times a second, and WCAG 2.3.1 only permits that below a 10%
 * relative-luminance swing. --ink-figure sits at 7.6% against the ink ground;
 * --primary-dark is 11.0% and --primary is 22.1%, and either would flash for
 * an audience aged 13-18. Detail can grow. Brightness cannot.
 */
